purpose: Deterministic test package catalog for capturing plaintext state, validating canonical encrypted scrambling state, validating recovered plaintext state, and exercising validator failures without creating a second encryption implementation.

stateModel.requirement: Capture normalized input bits, source digest, canonical key, and effective key configuration before encryption.

Capture the canonical encrypted package, validate package/key binding and deterministic replay through the Binary Cube engine, and record scrambling-quality observations separately from method validity.
Decrypt the captured encrypted package with the captured key and require exact payload, length, and digest equivalence to the pre-encryption capture.

positiveCases.description: Canonical four-cell baseline aligned with the portable self-test family.
Minimum legal grid with a one-bit payload and heavy deterministic filler pressure.
Low-entropy all-zero input intended to expose statistical leakage or weak scrambling characteristics.
Low-entropy all-one input paired with a different face family.
Highly regular alternating input for transition-pattern leakage testing.
Repeated structured byte pattern for block repetition and pattern-preservation observations.
Sparse payload mask designed to exercise multi-block filler behavior and package sizing.
Full mask configuration minimizing filler cells while spanning multiple blocks.
Quarter-turn normalization and perpendicular-face transform exercise.
Human-entered binary input containing whitespace; state one must capture the normalized canonical bitstream.

negativeCases.description: Empty payload must be rejected before encryption.
Non-binary payload characters must be rejected before encryption.
Grid size below the canonical minimum must be rejected.
Identical input/output faces must be rejected.
Opposite input/output faces must be rejected because they preserve the original projection.
A ciphertext mutation must fail canonical package validation.
Truncated ciphertext must fail encrypted-state validation.
Checksum tampering must be rejected by the package validator.
Package/key identity mismatch must be rejected.
Unknown package format must be rejected.
A separately valid but incorrect key must not decrypt the captured package.
Tampered key fingerprint must fail before decryption.
Tampered SHA-256 key digest must fail before decryption.
A key with no payload cells must fail structural validation.
A non-permutation row map must fail key validation.

scramblingObservations.interpretation: Method validity establishes that the package is a canonical Binary Cube transformation. Quality signals look for weaknesses and are intentionally reported separately so pathological inputs can reveal weaknesses without being mistaken for an unrelated algorithm.
